solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Part of a striker’s game, to persevere (10)

annotation.definitionNote: A matchstick is the shaft of a match, the 'striker'.

blocks.note: to stick at something = to persevere

annotation.surface: A footballer's performance and the need to keep going.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Striker' looks like a footballer, but here it is a match, the thing you strike to light; its stick is part of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A match is struck, so it is a striker, and its wooden stick is the matchstick.

entries.clue: Active way of working on hostility (6)

blocks.note: MO = modus operandi, Latin for 'way of working'

annotation.surface: A description of an energetic but aggressive working style.
annotation.walkthrough: MO is the police abbreviation for modus operandi, a criminal's habitual method.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a person able to move about freely and get around is active.

entries.clue: Bug found by a famous model’s PA (6)

indicatorNotes.found by: the bug is found beside the model, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: the Model T Ford, the most famous car model

annotation.surface: A supermodel's personal assistant discovers a listening device.
annotation.walkthrough: PA reads as a personal assistant but is a public-address system; Tannoy is the British trade name for one, used generically for station loudspeakers.
annotation.definitionFit: A Tannoy is a public-address (PA) loudspeaker system.

entries.clue: Rwanda has ill-prepared border protection (8,4)

indicatorNotes.prepared: letters prepared are made ready, put into a new state

annotation.surface: An African country's frontier defences are not ready.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ill-prepared' reads as one word, but it splits: ILL is fodder and 'prepared' rearranges it. Hadrian's Wall is the Roman wall across northern England.
annotation.definitionFit: Hadrian's Wall was built to protect Roman Britain's northern border.

entries.clue: Small creature with digits for ears (4)

indicatorNotes.for ears: what the ears hear rather than what is written

annotation.surface: An odd little animal whose ears are replaced by fingers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Digits' suggests fingers, but toes are digits too, and 'toed' says the same as the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by type: this warty amphibian is one small creature among many.

entries.clue: Particles in a stream or river in China (7,3)

blocks.note: the Oder, a European river on the German-Polish border

annotation.surface: Something floating in a Chinese stream or river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stream' pretends to be water, but it is a flow of electrons.
annotation.definitionFit: Physics sense: the ray from a cathode is a beam of electrons, and the clue describes what it is made of.

entries.clue: Stocking fillers on front of sleigh (4)

indicatorNotes.front of: the front of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

annotation.surface: Christmas presents stuffed into the stocking at the front of Santa's sleigh.
annotation.walkthrough: Stocking fillers sounds like Christmas presents, but it is what actually fills a stocking when worn. Cricket's leg side is also called the on side.
annotation.definitionFit: Legs are what fill stockings when they are worn.

entries.clue: Number in Labour calling for an injection of backbone (8)

blocks.note: read NUMB-er: something that numbs pain during childbirth
an anaesthetic injected into the spine, the backbone

annotation.surface: A Labour MP demands the party find some courage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a count and 'Labour' as the party; read NUMB-er, and labour as childbirth. 'Backbone' is courage on the surface, the spine underneath.
annotation.definitionFit: An epidural is a spinal anaesthetic injection used to numb pain in childbirth.

entries.clue: Left unfinished, wine is returned (8)

indicatorNotes.unfinished: the wine loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.returned: sent back, so read right to left

blocks.note: RETSINA, a Greek wine, without its final A

annotation.surface: A half-drunk bottle of wine is sent back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left unfinished' reads as one phrase, but 'Left' is the definition and 'unfinished' works on the wine; the whole string then turns round. Sinister is Latin for left, used in heraldry.
annotation.definitionFit: In heraldry sinister means the left side of a shield.

entries.clue: American checks boats on edge of a river delta (4,6)

indicatorNotes.on: the boats are placed after the other pieces

blocks.note: a river's edge is its bank
Delta is D in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An American inspects boats moored at the edge of a river delta.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Checks' looks like a verb but is the American spelling of cheques, and 'delta' is not the river's mouth but the letter D.
annotation.definitionFit: A bank draft is a cheque drawn by a bank, spelt check in American usage.

entries.clue: A dictator’s cruel appearance (4)

indicatorNotes.A dictator’s: a dictator here is someone dictating, speaking words aloud to be written

annotation.surface: A tyrant has a brutal look.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' reads as a tyrant, but it is someone who dictates, speaking a word for someone else to spell.
annotation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or bearing.

entries.clue: Huge spirit shown by top athlete (6,6)

blocks.note: a triple is a treble measure of spirits
a jumper is a top, a sweater

annotation.surface: A champion sportsman shows great strength of character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' reads as determination, but it is a drink: a triple is three measures. A jumper is the British word for a sweater.
annotation.definitionFit: A triple jumper competes in the triple jump, an athletics event.

entries.clue: Ladies relatives visit, but not for long (4,2)

blocks.note: the Ladies is a women's toilet, a loo

annotation.surface: Female relations drop by for a short stay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' reads as women, but in Britain the Ladies is the women's toilet, and loo is everyday British for toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: To look in on someone is to pay them a brief visit.

entries.clue: Crab starter to spoil the family cat (8)

indicatorNotes.starter to: the starter of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the family's cat is our cat

annotation.surface: A crab appetiser made to tempt the household cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crab starter' looks like a seafood course, but Crab is a grumpy person and 'starter' goes with 'to spoil'.
annotation.definitionFit: A crab is a crabby, bad-tempered person, a sourpuss.

entries.clue: Fantastic Four infiltrating premises in disguise (10)

indicatorNotes.infiltrating: the Four gets inside the other letters

annotation.surface: Superheroes sneaking into a building undercover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic Four' reads as the superhero team, but 'Fantastic' is the definition and the Four is Roman IV.
annotation.definitionFit: Fantastic and impressive both mean remarkably good.

entries.clue: No power? Dead motor needs this (6,5)

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
the late X = X, now dead

annotation.surface: A car with a flat battery won't start.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a breakdown, but a motor (car) needs a number plate to be on the road.
annotation.definitionFit: Every motor car must carry a number plate showing its registration.

entries.clue: A horse — one always turning circles in pain (8)

indicatorNotes.circles: to circle something is to surround it, so the turned word goes round the one

blocks.note: gee-gee, a child's word for a horse

annotation.surface: A horse, forever going round in circles, suffers pain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pain' is a verb here, to hurt or distress, not the horse's suffering.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to pain someone is to distress or wrong them, the sense of this word.

entries.clue: Fish gumbo, originally two other fish (8)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally = at its origin, its first letter

blocks.note: ray and ling are both fish

annotation.surface: A seafood stew recipe using three kinds of fish.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'fish' twice on purpose: once as the definition, once to name the two fish in the wordplay. Ling is a long cod-like sea fish.
annotation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

entries.clue: Battling with bugs, a farmer grew bananas (4,7)

indicatorNotes.bananas: bananas = crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A farmer fighting pests while growing a banana crop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' reads as crop pests, but here they are germs; 'bananas' is not the crop but the signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Germ warfare is fighting with disease organisms, bugs, as weapons.

entries.clue: Snowman’s extremities drip and drop off (6)

indicatorNotes.extremities: the extremities of a word are its ends

blocks.note: first and last letters of snowman

annotation.surface: A snowman melting at the edges until bits fall off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drop off' looks like melting pieces falling, but it means fall asleep.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to drop off is to nod off, fall into a light sleep.

entries.clue: Facing a group of offensive ne’er-do-wells (6)

indicatorNotes.a group of: a group of letters taken from within the words

annotation.surface: Confronting a gang of nasty good-for-nothings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facing' reads as confronting, but it is a noun: a surface layer.
annotation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin facing layer over a surface.

entries.clue: Heavyweight Tory’s arranged robes for the king (8)

annotation.definitionNote: A royalist is someone for the king; the answer is a noun, the definition a phrase.

indicatorNotes.robes: wraps around, as a robe does

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali, world heavyweight boxing champion

annotation.surface: A Conservative big hitter lays out the king's regalia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Robes' reads as royal garments, but it is a verb: the arranged letters clothe ALI.
annotation.definitionFit: A supporter of the monarchy takes the crown's side, so is for the king.

entries.clue: One in five ice cream centres is fruit (6)

indicatorNotes.centres: the middle letter of each word

blocks.note: a quin is a quintuplet, one of five born together
middle letters of iCe and crEam

annotation.surface: A dessert statistic: a fifth of ice creams have a fruit filling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ice cream centres' reads as a filling, but it takes the middle letter of each word.
annotation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, pear-shaped fruit.

entries.clue: Judgement I must leave unvoiced (4)

indicatorNotes.must leave: the I departs from the word

annotation.surface: Someone forced to leave a verdict unspoken.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unvoiced' reads as a verdict kept quiet, but it is the word for unspoken, which gives up its I.
annotation.definitionFit: Tact is sensitive judgement in dealing with people.

entries.clue: English team leader on the way out (4)

indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI
first letter of 'the', placed on (after) the rest

annotation.surface: The England captain is about to lose the job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Team leader' reads as the captain, but 'leader' belongs to 'the'; 'on the way out' splits after 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the door or passage you leave a building by.

entries.clue: Think badly of fool for entering seedy bar (10)

indicatorNotes.entering: the pieces go inside the bar

blocks.note: a dive is a seedy bar

annotation.surface: Someone frowns on a fool going into a disreputable pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a mere link word, but it does work as a synonym for 'in favour of'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hold an unfavourable opinion of something.

entries.clue: Bite lip (4)

blocks.note: bite = sharpness, as in a remark with bite
lip = rim, as in the lip of a cup

annotation.surface: An instruction to stop yourself from speaking.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like verbs about the mouth; both are nouns here.
annotation.definitionFit: Edge covers both sharpness (a voice with an edge has bite) and the rim of something (its lip).

entries.clue: East Rye, twice rebuilt in the past (10)

indicatorNotes.twice: twice means two times over, so RYE is written out two times before rearranging
indicatorNotes.rebuilt: the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder: EAST plus RYE twice, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A town in Sussex that has been rebuilt twice over its history.
annotation.walkthrough: Rye is a small historic town in East Sussex, so 'East Rye' reads as a place; 'twice' doubles RYE.
annotation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means the past, times gone by.
